module_title: Sectoral State Initiatives - Women Empowerment, Health, and Public Grievance Portals
introduction: This level transitions to high-impact sectoral initiatives. States have developed unique portals for grievance redressal and massive localized health and women-centric DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer) schemes that operate parallel to, or enhance, central schemes.

core_concepts.title: Jan Aadhaar Yojana (Rajasthan)
core_concepts.description:
- Core Objective: Replaced the Bhamashah Yojana. It acts as a single-number, single-card, single-identity system for the entire family.
- Unique Feature: The female head of the family is declared as the primary cardholder, and all direct benefit transfers (pensions, rations, scholarships) are routed exclusively through her bank account to promote women's financial empowerment.

core_concepts.title: Mission Shakti (Uttar Pradesh)
core_concepts.description:
- Core Objective: An umbrella initiative focusing on the safety, dignity, and empowerment of women and girls in the state.
- Implementation: Combines strict law enforcement (anti-Romeo squads, fast-track courts) with awareness campaigns and the establishment of women help desks in every police station.

core_concepts.title: CM Helpline & Public Grievance Portals
core_concepts.description:
- **Jan Sunwai (Uttar Pradesh)**: An integrated system for grievance redressal (IGRS) where citizens can track their complaints online.
- **CM Window (Haryana)**: A web portal allowing citizens to register their grievances directly to the Chief Minister's Office, ensuring strict monitoring and time-bound disposal by respective departments.

core_concepts.title: Chiranjeevi Health Insurance Scheme (Rajasthan)
core_concepts.description:
- Core Objective: A universal health coverage scheme that provided cashless treatment up to ₹25 Lakhs (initially ₹5L, later upgraded) to all families in the state.
- Significance: It went beyond the central Ayushman Bharat scheme by covering the *entire population* of the state rather than just the BPL/vulnerable categories.

important_entities.name: Integrated Grievance Redressal System (IGRS)
important_entities.significance: IGRS portals like Jan Sunwai link local block offices directly to the State Secretariat. They auto-escalate complaints to higher authorities if a local officer fails to resolve the issue within the stipulated timeframe.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Do not confuse UIDAI's 'Aadhaar' with Rajasthan's 'Jan Aadhaar'. Central Aadhaar is an **individual** identity number. Jan Aadhaar is a **family** identity number used specifically for state-level welfare targeting.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: UP Listens (Sunwai), Haryana Opens a Window.
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Quickly binds the Jan Sunwai portal to Uttar Pradesh (Sunwai means to listen/hearing) and the CM Window portal to Haryana.

exam_strategy_tips: In UPSC Prelims, questions often test the comparative scope of schemes. If a statement says 'Ayushman Bharat provides the highest insurance cover among all state and central schemes,' it is incorrect, as state schemes like Rajasthan's Chiranjeevi offered much higher ceilings.
